name: Canada Nature Fund for Aquatic Species at Risk
summary: Multi-year, multi-partner stewardship projects that recover and protect aquatic species at risk in Canada, with about $15.5 million a year available in the fourth round (2027-2031). Indigenous-led projects are prioritised.

eligibility.rule: Benefits multiple aquatic species at risk: one SARA-listed and another SARA-listed or COSEWIC-assessed
Directly addresses recovery measures in existing federal aquatic species at risk recovery documents
Engages multiple partners providing financial or in-kind project support
Is implemented between April 1, 2027 and March 31, 2031
Plans to share project information and results publicly or with other CNFASAR recipients

status.quote: Funding is now available for projects that can be completed by March 31, 2031.

deadline.quote: by November 16, 2026, at 23:59 (Pacific time). Proposals received after this time will not be considered.

pool.quote: A total of $15.5 million is available under the program each fiscal year of this round.

applicant_types.quote: Research, academic and educational institutions Canadian individuals For-profit organizations, such as small businesses with less than 500 employees, companies, corporations, and industry associations Local organizations such as community associations and groups

access.quote: project leads must complete a project proposal form and email it to the regional coordinator in the region in which the proposed project will be implemented

window.quote: Funding is now available under the fourth round of CNFASAR (2027-2031).

amount.quote: Projects are generally expected to range from $500,000 to $5 million in total, over 4 years.

geography.quote: Other costs that support the conservation and protection of Canada's fish, fish habitat, and aquatic species at risk

co_finance_required.quote: Although a 1:1 funding match is not required, proponents must identify project partners and outline their respective cash and/or in-kind contributions to the project.

effort.quote: To apply for this funding, project leads must complete a project proposal form and email it to the regional coordinator in the region in which the proposed project will be implemented by November 16, 2026, at 23:59 (Pacific time).

eligibility.quote: Meaningfully benefit multiple aquatic species at risk, including a minimum of one Species at Risk Act (SARA) aquatic listed species (or designatable unit), and at least one other SARA-listed or at-risk Committee on the Status of Endangered Wildlife in Canada (COSEWIC) assessed species (or designatable unit).
Directly address recovery measures set out in existing federal aquatic species at risk recovery documents (available on the SARA Public Registry).

Engage multiple partners. A partner is defined as a person or organization that provides financial or in-kind support to the project, such as activity planning, activity development and implementation.
Be implemented between April 1, 2027 and March 31, 2031.
Plan to share project information and results publicly and/or with other CNFASAR recipients.
